answer.rationale: Timeline is the strongest signal available: the release landed ~2h ago and write-path p99 began climbing ~90m ago, so the release is the leading (not proven) hypothesis, and rollback is the only candidate that removes a suspected cause rather than masking symptoms. I want memory_b1 verified because it is the direct precedent for 'rollback cleared the incident' — but its archived record is about a checkout error spike, not write-path latency under settlement peak, and I need to know whether the rollback there was performed under heavy write load or in a quiet window; if it was quiet, its reassurance does not transfer. I want memory_b6 verified because it partly contradicts the hypothesis: if staged gating and canary cohorts reliably surface regressions inside an hour, a bad build should have been caught pre-GA, which would either weaken release-causation or reveal that gating was bypassed for this release — either answer changes the decision materially. Alternatives considered and set aside: route_read_replicas (memory_b5) addressed read/dashboard contention on the primary, and this is a write-heavy settlement peak, so the mechanism likely does not apply; add_capacity (memory_b3) worked when the load was anticipated and provisioned ahead, not mid-incident, and provisioning latency is poor against a 90-minute climb; regional_failover (memory_b2) moves a release-induced defect with the traffic and risks in-flight write loss; enable_circuit_breaker (memory_b4) contained an external partner fault, and failing fast on our own write path would shed exactly the customer writes the objective forbids losing. Downstream risk flagged: a rollback executed at settlement peak can strand or duplicate in-flight writes, and schema or data-format changes shipped with the release may not be backward-compatible — this is why I want a small guarded rollback (single cell or cohort, drain-then-rollback, write-loss counters and p99 watched for a short bake) before any fleet-wide action, rather than committing the one available intervention to an irreversible broad move. I am also aware these inherited notes are outcome summaries, each recording a success; the archive is thin on cases where these actions failed, so I am treating their base rates as optimistic. If verification shows b1's rollback occurred under low write load or b6 shows gating was actually applied and clean, I would drop release-causation, hold the intervention, and spend the window on diagnosis of the write path instead.
